newsitem.title: FRANCE: Argentina seen well placed in Algeria wheat tender.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seen well placed in Algeria wheat tender.

text.p: Cheaper Argentine wheat stands a better chance to be selected over other origins at a tender Algeria launched for 100,000 tonnes of optional wheat, traders said on Tuesday.

Algeria was still negotiating the purchase of the wheat, one day after launching a snap tender for 100,00 tonnes of U.S. and/or French and/or Argentine soft wheat for shipment in the second half of December, they said.
"Algeria seems to be focusing on Argentine wheat because it is cheaper," one trader told Reuters.
Traders submitted bids on Monday with results expected later in the day or by tomorrow.
Exporters have linked the new tender to recent sales of U.S. and French wheat to Egypt at prices they described as "very low".
Argentine wheat is five to seven dollars cheaper than French wheat, which is currently worth $166 per tonne, including freight, but excluding the cost of a Coface export credit, one trader said.
On Saturday Egypt bought 150,000 tonnes of French soft wheat at prices ranging from $146 to $147 per tonne, Fob. Argentine wheat is currently worth $133-$134 per tonne, Fob.
